## Purpose and annotation questions

This pilot evaluates the reproducibility of continuous physician probability ratings for two
separated assessments:

- **Image rating:** the probability that the current chest radiograph shows bilateral pulmonary
  opacities or infiltrates meeting the ARDS imaging criterion.
- **Report rating:** the probability that the radiology report states or implies the same finding.

Ratings remain on their original 0-100 scale. The analysis estimates agreement and alignment; it
does not evaluate an NLP model or treat either assessment as a perfect gold standard.

```{python}

```

## Configuration and input files

Rater identity is supplied by the configured file-to-rater mapping. It is never inferred from row
order, timestamps, or filenames. The report-text field is discarded during ingestion before the
analysis tables are created.

```{python}
display(

        result.input_qa_summary["check"].isin(

                "configured_raters",
                "source_case_rater_rows",
                "unique_cases",
                "cases_present_for_all_raters",
            ]
        )
    ].reset_index(drop=True)
)
```

## Data validation and completeness

Only ratings with the corresponding REDCap completion value of `2` and a valid value from 0 to
100 enter the analysis. Incomplete and unverified ratings are audited but excluded.

```{python}
display(result.input_qa_summary.reset_index(drop=True))
display(result.case_coverage_by_rater.reset_index(drop=True))
```

## Image inter-rater agreement

ICC(2,1) estimates absolute agreement for one physician rating. ICC(2,k) estimates reliability of
the mean across all configured physicians. ICC calculations use only cases completed by every
rater; pairwise differences use all cases shared by each pair. Correlations describe association,
not agreement.

```{python}
display(
    result.rater_descriptive_summary[
        result.rater_descriptive_summary["task"] == "image"
    ].reset_index(drop=True)
)
display(
    result.interrater_agreement_summary[
        result.interrater_agreement_summary["task"] == "image"
    ].reset_index(drop=True)
)
display(
    result.pairwise_rater_agreement[
        result.pairwise_rater_agreement["task"] == "image"
    ].reset_index(drop=True)
)
display(Image(data=result.figure_paths["image_ratings_by_case"].read_bytes(), format="png"))
```

## Image-report alignment

The primary comparison uses case-level means only when all configured physicians completed both
tasks. Positive signed differences indicate that the mean report rating exceeded the mean image
rating. Bootstrap confidence intervals resample cases.

```{python}
display(result.image_report_alignment_summary.reset_index(drop=True))
display(result.within_rater_image_report_alignment.reset_index(drop=True))
display(Image(data=result.figure_paths["image_report_scatter"].read_bytes(), format="png"))
display(Image(data=result.figure_paths["image_report_bland_altman"].read_bytes(), format="png"))
```

## Interpretation and pilot limitations

Continuous ratings are the primary measurements. ICC and difference metrics assess agreement;
correlation alone does not. Image-report comparisons measure alignment between assessments based
on different information sources, not accuracy against a perfect reference test.

These pilot estimates are expected to be imprecise with approximately 50 cases and three raters.
The raters may not represent all clinicians, and image and report ratings are not interchangeable.
No annotation-duration analysis is possible without explicit timing fields or REDCap audit-log
data. This notebook does not evaluate any NLP model.
